Brazil welcomes strengthened cooperation between the Office of the Prosecutor and Libyan authorities and a more positive trajectory. Complementarity is central: national jurisdictions have the primary duty; the ICC acts only when a State is unable or unwilling. Nonparties have no Rome Statute obligations, yet Resolution 1970 (2011) under Chapter VII requires Libyan authorities to cooperate fully. Other States and organizations are urged to cooperate; the ICC has no enforcement instruments and depends on States, so requests must conform to the Statute and relevant Council resolutions.

No ICC judgments exist in the Libyan situation. We welcome evidence collection and investigative progress. For transparency, we request additional information on the four key lines of inquiry. We hope fruitful OTP-Libyan relations can deliver justice and accountability under complementarity.

For this workshop exercise, workplan R emphasizes cooperation and a public update but lacks a channel for victims, witnesses and their representatives inside and outside Libya and does not request line-by-line progress on the four inquiries. I recommend a protected two-way channel accessible to those groups and a line-by-line update. Expanded outreach and reporting require staff and witness-privacy safeguards; narrower outreach costs less but risks selectivity. These are analytical recommendations, not a Brazilian endorsement of R or a future vote.<|im_end|>
